text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm plans to give increased authority to STE securities board. (p1)
- Consumer packaging helps push up Van Leer first half net by more than 20 pct to Dfl 45.4 million. (p1)
- FNV union criticizes cabinet's planned changes to public health insurance scheme. (p1)
- Bedroom chain Beter Bed plans bourse listing. (p1)
- Machine maker Nedschroef posts 15 pct higher first half net on seven percent turnover growth. (p3)
- Technical wholesaler Otra puts aside Dfl 41.1 million for restructuring its British and German units. (p3)
- Chemist co-op OPG unsure about year profit due to health minister's drugs price measures. (p4)
- Automation firm Cap Gemini (former Cap Volmac) sees solid turnover and profits growth. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Libertel to charge mobile phone calls per second. (p2)
- Single premium insurances more popular than ever with 100,000 sold in first six months. (p2)
- Kas-Ass Bank books 93 pct higher first half net. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- At least five options traders suspected in BolsWessanen insider trading case. (p23)
- Auto-dealer Athlon first half net up by 11 pct. (p23)
- Builder HBG's Tebodin unit takes over Czech's Projekta.
- Entrepreneur Rosen Jacobson buys 95 pct stake in Belgium's Vlaamse Luchttransport Maatschapplij VLM. (p27)
TROUW
- Liberal (VVD) leader Frits Bolkestein fears higher interest rates after introduction of European single currency.
- Tobacco industry furious at cabinet for violating earlier agreements to not raise excise duties. (p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Employment in Rotterdam area grew 0.8 pct in 1995. (p15)
- Employers association VNO-NCW sees continuing economic growth in 1996 and 1997. (p15)
